title: aurora-insurance-integration-call-notes-2026-04-18
content:
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood CSM), Dr. Emily Park (Aurora technical lead), Marcus Wei (Aurora product), Claire Huang (Aurora security)

High-level goal: Aurora wants to embed contextual policy-question answering into their claims intake flow to reduce first-touch SLA from 24h to <4h for straightforward queries and to triage complex cases to human adjusters. Initial scope: NLU-based Q&A + recommended next-step classification, not full claim ingestion in v1.

Call summary / notes to self:
- Aurora is time-sensitive: they want an initial internal pilot within 6 weeks. Their pilot dataset = anonymized claims Q&A logs (~12k rows).
- Two main integration paths discussed: 1) Server-side synchronous API calls from their intake app for short questions (low-latency), 2) Async batch scoring for nightly enrichment of open claims. They prefer 1) for MVP.
- Data residency: Aurora requires that all PII stays within their VPC. They are evaluating the Redwood Private option (VPC + customer-managed control plane). Claire emphasized KMS integration and audit logs as must-haves.
- Security: They will require SOC2 + additional attestation and default encryption-at-rest keys under their KMS. Need to confirm HSM support timeline.
- Model/quality: Aurora expects deterministic-ish answers for policy lookup; high hallucination risk is a blocker. We suggested retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a conservative answer fallback of "refer to human" when confidence < threshold. Marcus asked about latency with RAG — we estimated 250–450ms additional retrieval time depending on vector DB location and shard size.
- Throughput: Pilot traffic estimate = 10 rps peak, 1–2k q/day. Production could be 80–120 rps. They want clear cost estimates for both Dedicated and Hosted options.

Technical requirements / clarifications needed:
1) Data pipeline: exact format of citations / snippets they want surfaced in the UI (snippet length, token budget, citation links). Need sample anonymized records (~50 rows) to validate retrieval heuristics. ACTION: Jordan to request samples.
2) PII handling: confirm which fields are considered PII. Claire will share Aurora's data classification doc (expected by 2026-04-22).
3) Auth & networking: For Private deployment we need their VPC CIDR, VPN/IH tunnel details, and KMS ARNs. For Hosted, they want to know if partial PII redaction is acceptable.
4) Eval metrics: define success for pilot — suggested: top-1 exact match on policy clause extraction (aim >= 75%), human escalation rate < 20%, median latency < 600ms. Marcus to confirm KPIs by next week.

Known gotchas / risks:
- Hallucination risk if docs not curated. Recommend canonical policy store + aggressive retrieval scoring + answer-abstain policy.
- Cost surprises from high token context windows if Aurora tries to push full claim histories; need guardrails in prompt design and token limits.
- VPC provisioning timelines can add 2–3 weeks; flagging in project plan.
- They use an internal vector DB (Milvus) — we'll need to validate compatibility with our native RAG connectors or consider a lightweight replication into supported managed vector store.

Action items / next steps (owners & rough ETA):
- Jordan: Request 50 anonymized sample Q&A logs + sample policy PDFs (due 2026-04-20).
- Claire (Aurora): Share data classification doc + list of PII fields (due 2026-04-22).
- Sofia: Prepare pilot cost estimate (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with 3 traffic scenarios (MVP, scaled, peak) — rough draft by 2026-04-23.
- Alex: Draft recommended RAG architecture diagram and latency/cost tradeoffs (due 2026-04-21).
- Engineering spike: Validate Milvus connector + sample retrieval latency with 50k embedding vectors (internal ticket AI-872). Spike owner: Alex, ETA 1 week.
- Security: Confirm HSM/KMS support for Private; escalate to security team if timeline > 2 weeks.

Meeting follow-up plan:
- Short internal sync (Redwood SE + CSM + Eng) tomorrow to align on asks and confirm which samples we need.
- Customer follow-up call scheduled for 2026-04-26 to review architecture options and cost estimates. Tentative time: 10am PT.

Notes / informal thoughts:
- Consider offering a temporary Hosted isolated environment with strict token redaction for faster pilot if Private provisioning slips. Use a synthetic dataset to demo UI.
- Could propose a conservative default policy: do not synthesize policy clauses across multiple docs — surface source snippet + link instead. Lowers hallucination and legal exposure.
- If Aurora wants citations visible to end-users, we'll need per-token accounting for what we send back; check Console limits for retention and PII masking.

Draft email to send after doc samples arrive (copy to Claire & Marcus):
Subject: Next steps — Aurora pilot samples and architecture options
Hi Claire / Marcus — thanks again for the call. We're prepping a short pilot plan and would appreciate the 50 anonymized Q&A rows and two sample policy PDFs so we can validate retrieval and prompt templates. Jordan/Sofia will share a short architecture note and cost comparison by next week. If Private/VPC is required, could you also share your VPN contact and KMS ARNs?

Action: Draft + send after samples received.

Tags for internal tracking: #aurora #pilot #RAG #private-deployments
